questions.knowledge_point: Finding a Power of a Matrix
questions.worked_solution:
To find ${P}^{2},$ we multiply $P$ by itself:

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{2} & =P\cdot P \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 6 & -4 \\ -1 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}-X-2 \\  & ={X}^{2}-X-2I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(D)={D}^{2}-D-2I.$

Let's calculate ${D}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}^{2} & =D\cdot D \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -8 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(D):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(D) & ={D}^{2}-D-2I \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -8 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -8 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}9-3-2 & -8-(-2)-0 \\ 0-0-0 & 1-1-2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -6 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}^{2} & =D\cdot D \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ -6 & -4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ -6 & -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & =-{X}^{2}+3X+2 \\  & =-{X}^{2}+3X+2I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(D)=-D^2+3D+2I.$

Let's calculate $D^2$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}^{2} & =D\cdot D \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -10 \\ 0 & 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
